subject: pharmacology
title: Other antibacterials: fluoroquinolones, vancomycin, metronidazole and UTI drugs

steps.tx: **Fluoroquinolones** such as ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin block bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase enzymes. They treat urinary infection and anthrax, while respiratory agents cover atypical pneumonia pathogens in adults. The class carries **tendinopathy**, aortic dissection risk, QT prolongation and worsening of myasthenia gravis. Children usually avoid these drugs because cartilage toxicity concerns limit paediatric use in practice. Iron and antacids block absorption, so patients must space cations away from each dose.
steps.say: Fluoroquinolones block bacterial DNA enzymes and they treat urinary infection and anthrax in adults treated. Respiratory agents cover atypical pneumonia pathogens while other members treat complicated urinary infections in hospitals daily. The class carries tendinopathy and aortic risk so clinicians reserve it for selected infections only. Children usually avoid these drugs because cartilage toxicity is a concern that limits paediatric use in practice today. Iron and antacids block absorption so patients must space cations away from each dose.

steps.tx: **Metronidazole** kills anaerobes above and below the diaphragm and it also treats amoebic and Giardia infections. Alcohol during treatment provokes a **disulfiram like reaction** with vomiting, so patients must abstain completely. Vancomycin treats resistant Gram positive infection intravenously and treats colonic infection when given orally. Rapid vancomycin infusion causes **red man syndrome**, which slowing the infusion and antihistamine cover prevent effectively. Modern dosing follows exposure monitoring rather than simple trough targets in most hospitals.
steps.say: Metronidazole kills anaerobes and it also treats amoebic and Giardia infections in patients presenting clinically. Alcohol during treatment provokes vomiting and flushing so patients must abstain completely during therapy courses. Vancomycin treats resistant Gram positive infection intravenously and it treats colonic infection when given orally. Rapid infusion causes flushing of the neck and slowing the infusion prevents that reaction effectively. Modern dosing follows exposure monitoring because kidney injury rises with excessive drug exposure overall.

steps.tx: **Daptomycin** treats resistant Gram positive bacteraemia and endocarditis but it never treats pneumonia in patients. Pulmonary surfactant binds and inactivates the drug inside alveoli, so the **lungs fail** as a site every time. Weekly muscle enzyme checks watch for myopathy, especially when patients also take statin drugs. The combination drug for urinary infection also covers Pneumocystis and Nocardia in selected patients. Nitrofurantoin treats cystitis only because it never reaches kidney tissue or blood adequately.
steps.say: Daptomycin treats resistant Gram positive bacteraemia and endocarditis but it never treats pneumonia in patients admitted. Pulmonary surfactant binds the drug and it inactivates the drug inside alveoli very effectively there. Weekly muscle enzyme checks watch for myopathy especially when patients also take statin drugs concurrently. Nitrofurantoin is limited to cystitis only because it never reaches kidney tissue or blood adequately in patients. The urinary combination drug also covers Pneumocystis pneumonia in selected immunocompromised patients needing treatment.

steps.tx: This chest radiograph shows bilateral peripheral infiltrates that the labels attribute to **eosinophilic pneumonia** during treatment. The picture reminds you that **daptomycin** cannot treat ordinary pneumonia because surfactant inactivates it in alveoli. The same patient still needs weekly muscle enzyme monitoring because the drug can injure skeletal muscle silently. New breathlessness with spreading peripheral shadowing during therapy should make you stop and rethink the drug. Examiners pair this radiograph with bacteraemia success and pulmonary failure in a single stem.
steps.say: This chest radiograph shows bilateral peripheral infiltrates during treatment with a drug that treats bacteraemia well. The picture reminds you that surfactant inactivates the drug inside alveoli so pneumonia never responds adequately. The same patient needs weekly muscle enzyme monitoring because skeletal muscle injury develops silently during therapy. New breathlessness with spreading peripheral shadowing should make you stop and rethink the drug immediately. This pairing is deliberate because examiners combine radiographic failure in lung with excellent bloodstream activity in a single stem often.

steps.tx: Reserve drugs such as colistin treat carbapenem resistant Gram negative infection when safer options fail completely. That rescue role carries a **nephrotoxicity** and neurotoxicity price that limits use in practice. **Stewardship** protects every antibacterial because resistance spreads faster than new drug development today. Teams take cultures before antibiotics, narrow therapy after early review and control the source surgically. Short defined courses cure most infections and they reduce resistance pressure across the hospital.
steps.say: Reserve drugs such as colistin treat resistant Gram negative infection when safer options fail completely in hospitals. That rescue role carries kidney and nerve toxicity so clinicians restrict use very carefully indeed. Stewardship protects every antibacterial because resistance spreads faster than new drug development today in practice. Teams take cultures before antibiotics and they narrow therapy after early review of results available. Short defined courses cure most infections and they reduce resistance pressure across the hospital wards.
